tei:titleStmt.tei:title: מִי אֵֽדֶר וָהוֹד
Mi Eder va-Hod — a piyyuṭ in Nishmat Kol Ḥai for Shabbat Bereshit and Shavuot, from the Maḥzor Worms

tei:div.tei:head: Mi Eder va-Hod — a piyyuṭ in Nishmat Kol Ḥai for Shabbat Bereshit and Shavuot, from the Maḥzor Worms

tei:lg.tei:l: ...All my bones say: Cause, who is like You?
Saving the poor from those stronger than them, and the poor and needy from their oppressor!
Who, upon whom are hidden majesty and illumination,
is like You on the day of the universe’s start of creation?
Who, clad in triumph, like a cloak subsumed,
is like You on the day that the flood generation was doomed?
Who, girt in strength,
is like You on the day of counsel of giving strength?
Who, pure as snow clad,
is like You on the day Bel is shamed and adread?
Who, arrayed in garb of a vengeful feel,
is like You on the day from Media you repaid with zeal?
Who, like a tallit robe of pleasant relief,
is like You on the day You aroused zeal for Greece’s chief?
Who, measured like armor of right,
is like You on the day forces are crushed by might?
Who, whose hat is a helmet of salvation
is like You on the day in each hour, of decoration?
Who, repaying in garments of red,
is like You on the day You strongly from Edom tread?
Who adorned in purple splendid,
is like You on the day ordered myriads commended?
Who, beautified in tightly wrapped capes
is like You on the day of ten garments of splendid shapes?
Who is akin to You and who is equal to You and who is comparable to You...

tei:note.tei:p: In Maḥzor Worms, a later handwritten note says ע׳׳כ — read until here. The next lines, up until resh, were not recited at the time of the marginal additions. Note that the vav verse is directly about the giving of the Torah, and thus stopping there makes sense for Shavuot.
Before this word, in Maḥzor Worms, is a later handwritten note which is blurry, but may read מוסיף — add. These final two lines were recited aloud before returning to Nishmat Kol Ḥai.
